sections.h2: What makes selling in Murfreesboro different?
sections.html:
Murfreesboro is the seat of Rutherford County, 34 miles southeast of downtown Nashville, and the Census Bureau puts its population at 171,178 as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 152,769 at the 2020 census. A seller here deals with the city's Tax Department, the Rutherford County Assessor and the county Register of Deeds in separate offices.

Median value of owner-occupied housing is $402,100, and 52.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. That leaves nearly half of homes rented or vacant, so tell any buyer early if tenants occupy your house.

sections.h2: What is Murfreesboro's history and geography?
sections.html:
The Tennessee General Assembly picked the site for the Rutherford County seat in October 1811, and the town was chartered in January 1812. It served as the state capital from 1818 to 1826 before Nashville took over. Murfreesboro is also the geographic center of Tennessee, and a stone marker on Old Lascassas Pike names the spot.

The Battle of Stones River, fought from December 31, 1862 to January 2, 1863, produced 23,515 casualties, and Stones River National Battlefield preserves the site. The West Fork of the Stones River runs through town beside a greenway, and Lytle Creek flows through downtown near Cannonsburgh Village. Interstates 24 and 840 and U.S. Routes 41, 70S and 231 cross the city.

sections.h2: Who employs Murfreesboro and how does that shape demand?
sections.html:
The city's 2023 annual financial report lists the top employers in Rutherford County, led by Nissan with about 8,000 workers. Middle Tennessee State University, one of the largest undergraduate universities in the state, is based in the city.

Census figures show a median household income of $80,108, a mean commute of 26.7 minutes and a bachelor's degree rate of 43.0 percent among adults 25 and older.

sections.h2: How do Murfreesboro housing costs compare in the Census data?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates:

  • Median value, owner-occupied homes: $402,100.
  • Median gross rent: $1,481 a month.
  • Households: 60,683.
  • Persons in poverty: 8.8 percent.
  • Land area: 62.89 square miles.

A city this size spans many price points, so a citywide median is a rough guide. A recent sale on your own street says more than any average.

sections.h2: Does Murfreesboro weather and storm history matter for a sale?
sections.html:
Murfreesboro has a humid subtropical climate with mild winters and hot, humid summers. Its wet season runs February through July, peaking in June at about 5.7 inches of rain, and the hardiness zone is 7. On April 10, 2009, a low-end EF4 tornado struck the fringes of the city, killing two people and injuring 41, with 117 homes destroyed and 292 heavily damaged.

If you have replaced a roof or repaired storm damage, keep the invoices and permit numbers together to hand to a buyer.

sections.h2: When are Murfreesboro city property taxes due?
sections.html:
The 2026 city tax bills were mailed and opened for payment on October 1, 2026, and they can be paid through February 28, 2027 with no interest. Starting March 1, 2027, unpaid base tax accrues interest at 1.5 percent per month or part of a month. City policy now sets a February 28 due date every year beginning with the 2025 tax year, and a postmark counts as proof of timely mailing. If February 28 lands on a weekend, you have until the next working day.

  • Online: murfreesborotntax.com, by card, PayPal or e-check. Card fees run about 2.5 percent plus $0.30, and e-check costs $1.50.
  • By mail: City of Murfreesboro, P.O. Box 1139, Murfreesboro, TN 37133-1139.
  • In person: City Hall Finance Department, first floor, 111 West Vine Street, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

The city accepts partial payments under set guidelines, and unpaid amounts go to Chancery Court at the proper deadline. The City Tax Department's number is (615) 893-5210.

sections.h2: Who handles Murfreesboro assessment questions and tax relief?
sections.html:
Billing questions go to the Rutherford County Assessor's Office at (615) 898-7750, because the county assessor sets the values the city bills on. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value under state law. Under the Comptroller's schedule, county boards of equalization convene each June 1, so ask the assessor for this year's appeal deadline.

The city takes part in Tennessee's Property Tax Freeze and Property Tax Relief programs for low-income seniors 65 and older and for disabled veterans. If you qualify, ask the City Tax Department how an application interacts with a sale before you list.

sections.h2: Which schools serve a Murfreesboro house?
sections.html: Murfreesboro City Schools runs prekindergarten through sixth grade, with 12 schools and about 8,800 students. Rutherford County Schools, with 50 schools and over 49,000 students, handles secondary grades. Ask the city school system which zone your address falls into before you advertise.

sections.h2: What permits and rental rules apply in Murfreesboro?
sections.html:
The Building and Codes Department adopted the 2024 building codes and handles plan review, inspections and certificates of occupancy. It opens at 8:00 a.m., inspectors are in the office from 8:00 to 8:45 a.m., and the counter stops taking payments at 4:00 p.m. The City Council has also adopted a schedule of development impact fees.

Short-term rental owners pay a 5 percent occupancy tax monthly to the county and city, plus state business and sales tax, and need a business license from the county clerk and the city at $15 each. Airbnb and VRBO hosts are included.

sections.h2: How does recording work at the Rutherford County Register of Deeds?
sections.html: The Register of Deeds is at 319 North Maple Street, Room 133. Under the office's posted recording policy, a document accompanied by $10 or less of extra payment is recorded and the overage retained by the office, while overpayments above $10 are refunded by check at the end of the month. A document submitted short of the required fees is returned the same day. The state realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 is paid by the grantee when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When do Murfreesboro city property taxes stop being interest-free?
faqs.a: After February 28, 2027 for the 2026 tax year. Interest starts March 1 at 1.5 percent per month or part of a month on the unpaid base tax. A weekend deadline moves to the next working day.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Murfreesboro city taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Partial payments are accepted if you follow the city's guidelines, and unpaid amounts are turned over to Chancery Court at the proper deadline. Call (615) 893-5210 to talk it through.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Murfreesboro assessment?
faqs.a: The Rutherford County Assessor's Office, (615) 898-7750. Questions about paying or about tax relief go to the City Tax Department at (615) 893-5210.

faqs.q: Is there help with property tax for seniors in Murfreesboro?
faqs.a: Yes. The city participates in Tennessee's Property Tax Freeze and Property Tax Relief programs for qualifying low-income owners 65 and older and for disabled veterans.

faqs.q: What do short-term rental owners owe in Murfreesboro?
faqs.a: A 5 percent occupancy tax paid monthly to the county and city, state sales tax and gross receipts business tax, and $15 business licenses from the county clerk and the city.
